title: Quasi-isomorphism of the normalized finite scalar pullback Roos map
statement: Let ell be prime, E and L finite extensions of Q_ell, iota an embedding, f : X → Y any scheme morphism, and P a termwise-flat K-flat complex of completed E-coefficient module sheaves [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined]. Let alpha be a strict tower map from ordinary scalar extension [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension, lem-weil-scalar-extension-composition] of the finite pullback reduction tower of P to the finite pullback reduction tower of the ordinary scalar extension of P. Suppose every level sends 1 tensor f*(1 tensor x) to f*(1 tensor (1 tensor x)). Let kappa be a chain map from scalar extension of the source Roos complex to the Roos complex of its scalar-extended tower, whose unshifted and shifted product coordinates are the images under scalar extension of the corresponding source projections. Then kappa followed by Roos(alpha) is a quasi-isomorphism. This statement concerns the specified chain map on one good representative; it neither constructs nor assumes any comparison in a derived category.

proof.text: The finite-filtration lemma makes the cone of the normalized tower comparison eventually nullhomotopic, hence zero in the derived category, before taking Roos complexes.

Completed integral finite freeness and the ordinary scalar functor formulas identify restriction of ordinary extension with the finite power functor. Finite powers preserve countable products. Restriction is conservative and preserves products, hence ordinary extension preserves countable products. In each degree the two Roos coordinates identify its diagonal comparison with the direct sum of the two invertible product comparisons. Joint monicity of these coordinates makes the specified kappa equal to this diagonal isomorphism.

Apply the general ringed strict-tower homotopy-limit theorem directly to the completed module sheaf category. Its evaluation isomorphism transports the cone transitions to zero, so it inverts the tower map. The explicit Roos derivation and the termwise limit comparison identify its derived functor with that homotopy-limit functor by uniqueness of right derived functors. Naturality transports invertibility back to the concrete shifted-cone map, and localization detects the required quasi-isomorphism. Countable exactness is the existing pro-etale exact-products result. Compose with the isomorphism kappa.

lean.statement:
theorem integralScalarPullbackRoosQuasiIso {X Y : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (P : CochainComplex (integralTowerModules l E Y) ℤ)
    (hP : integralOperationsGoodComplex l E Y P)
    (α : ((integralOperationsPullbackTowerFunctor l E f).obj P) ⋙
        (integralOrdinaryScalar l E L ι X).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ) ⟶
      (integralOperationsPullbackTowerFunctor l L f).obj
        (((integralOrdinaryScalar l E L ι Y).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P))
    (hα :
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (i : ℤ) (V : Y.ProEt)
        (x : (P.X i).val.obj (op V)),
        ((α.app (op n)).f i).val.app (op ((AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.proEtaleBaseChange f).obj V))
          (integralOrdinaryTensorSection l E L ι X
            (((integralOperationsPullbackLevel l E f n).obj P).X i)
            (op ((AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.proEtaleBaseChange f).obj V)) 1
            (integralOperationsPullbackGenerator l E f n
              (((unrestrictedIntegralFiniteComplex l E Y n).obj P).X i) V
              (unrestrictedIntegralTensorSection l E Y n (P.X i) (op V) 1 x))) =
        integralOperationsPullbackGenerator l L f n
          (((unrestrictedIntegralFiniteComplex l L Y n).obj
            (((integralOrdinaryScalar l E L ι Y).mapHomologicalComplex
              (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj P)).X i) V
          (unrestrictedIntegralTensorSection l L Y n
            ((integralOrdinaryScalar l E L ι Y).obj (P.X i)) (op V) 1
            (integralOrdinaryTensorSection l E L ι Y (P.X i) (op V) 1 x)))
    (κ : ((integralOrdinaryScalar l E L ι X).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj
        (integralOperationsRoos ((integralOperationsPullbackTowerFunctor l E f).obj P)) ⟶
      integralOperationsRoos (((integralOperationsPullbackTowerFunctor l E f).obj P) ⋙
        (integralOrdinaryScalar l E L ι X).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)))
    (hκ : let C := (integralOperationsPullbackTowerFunctor l E f).obj P
      let G := (integralOrdinaryScalar l E L ι X).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)
      (∀ n : ℕ, κ ≫ CochainComplex.mappingCocone.fst
          ((towerTransitionEndomorphism (K := fun n ↦ G.obj (C.obj (op n)))
            (integralOperationsTowerStep (C ⋙ G)))) ≫
          Pi.π (fun n ↦ (G).obj (C.obj (op n))) n =
        (G).map
          (CochainComplex.mappingCocone.fst
            ((towerTransitionEndomorphism (K := fun n ↦ C.obj (op n))
            (integralOperationsTowerStep C))) ≫
            Pi.π (fun n ↦ C.obj (op n)) n)) ∧
      (∀ (i j : ℤ) (h : i + -1 = j) (n : ℕ), κ.f i ≫
          (CochainComplex.mappingCocone.snd
            ((towerTransitionEndomorphism (K := fun n ↦ G.obj (C.obj (op n)))
            (integralOperationsTowerStep (C ⋙ G))))).v i j h ≫
          (Pi.π (fun n ↦ (G).obj
            (C.obj (op n))) n).f j =
        (integralOrdinaryScalar l E L ι X).map
          ((CochainComplex.mappingCocone.snd
            ((towerTransitionEndomorphism (K := fun n ↦ C.obj (op n))
            (integralOperationsTowerStep C)))).v i j h ≫
          (Pi.π (fun n ↦ C.obj (op n)) n).f j))) :
    QuasiIso (κ ≫ integralOperationsRoosMap α)
